text.p: Spanish bank Banco Santander SA will take over Mexico's Grupo Financiero Invermexico SA next year in exchange for a huge capital injection to save its troubled bank unit Banco Mexicano, banking authorities said on Thursday.

Santander will add $378.5 million in fresh capital to Banco Mexicano and take control of the financial group at the beginning of next year, the National Banking and Securities Commission said in a statement.
A total of $425 million in fresh capital will be added to Banco Mexicano, the banking commission said.

Of the $378.5 million from Santander, some $166 million will be subscribed as share capital and $212.5 million will be mandatorily convertible obligations placed on the open market. If they are not sold, Santander will purchase them, the statement said.
The remaining $47 million be injected by Invermexico shareholders.
Santander will also create reserve provisions at Invermexico equal to 100 percent of current capital at Banco Mexicano, the commission said.

For its part, Banco Mexicano will sell an additional $2.364 billion of its loan portfolio to the government's Fobaproa bank support fund. It has already sold about 7.3 billion pesos in past-due loans to the government, according to analysts.

Santander becomes the second foreign bank to take a majority stake in a Mexican financial group since Mexican law was changed in 1995, at the height of a peso crisis that forced local banks to tap billions of dollars in government support to survive.
